goal: Develop CGKN with the same tailored PMP, adaptive delivery, built-in quality, and enterprise-learning method that CGKN offers to generated projects.

tailoring.rationale: CGKN needs stable kernel, provider, evidence, and delivery governance while its product-management and generation capabilities evolve through tested increments.

success_metrics: CGKN self-hosting management artifacts validate against registered schemas.
The project-local skill can initialize, validate, and retrieve bounded project-management context.
No change creates a second Codex conversation generation route or delivery exit.
Every completed increment records measurable quality evidence and a retrospective.
fixed_constraints: Preserve the reviewed API/provider Codex conversation generation route.
Preserve whiteboard and agent_session shared communication.
Preserve local_packager as the only delivery exit.
Use only canonical formal evidence statuses.
Do not expose internal management jargon in normal customer replies.
escalation_thresholds: Escalate any proposed change to codex_conversation.py that expands its responsibility.
Escalate any fallback that could become an unregistered generation path.
Return an increment for rework when required quality evidence is absent.

product_backlog.title: Define and self-host the tailored PMP, agile, and quality method
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN contributors and agents use one registered, inspectable method for CGKN and generated projects.
acceptance_criteria: The method covers people and feedback, value delivery, governance, quality planning, assurance, control, and improvement.
Repository instructions require proportionate self-hosting for non-trivial CGKN work.
Management workflow states remain separate from formal evidence statuses.

product_backlog.title: Maintain bounded enterprise experience with usage outcomes
product_backlog.outcome: Projects retrieve relevant evidence-backed experience without receiving a large global context.
acceptance_criteria: Validated and approved experience requires evidence and applicability boundaries.
Retrieval excludes unrelated, candidate, and retired experience.
Each applied experience can record a project and iteration usage outcome.

product_backlog.title: Feed tailored management context into formal provider planning
product_backlog.outcome: Generated projects receive relevant backlog, quality, risk, and experience context through the existing librarian.
acceptance_criteria: Management context enters the existing provider route without a second planner or delivery route.
Leaf prompts receive only bounded directly relevant context.
Provider and delivery contract tests remain green.

product_backlog.title: Prove the method on the ACFV-scale generation ladder
product_backlog.outcome: The method demonstrates bounded context, incremental integration, and quality feedback at the requested project scale.
acceptance_criteria: Small, medium, and ACFV-scale trials use the same management contracts.
Injected interface and quality defects route to affected work only.
The final report distinguishes planning, implementation, quality, and delivery evidence.

product_backlog.title: Bound large Provider file leaves below the gateway timeout
product_backlog.outcome: High-complexity files are generated through deterministic owned submodules and a compatibility facade so each resumable Provider request remains inside the measured transport-safe region.
acceptance_criteria: High-complexity source entries with many public symbols expand deterministically into legal owned submodules plus a facade while preserving the original public path.
Provider file calls default to at most 5000 output tokens and explicitly reject length-truncated responses before publication.
Each generated submodule retains its own split-file checkpoint, interface feedforward, boundary receipt, and affected-only repair behavior.
The Codex conversation Provider validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public delivery gate, and delivery manifest route remains unchanged.

product_backlog.title: Generate and verify a complete CS2 demo integrity-analysis project
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN proves the bounded-leaf route on a substantial real project that imports authorized CS2 demos, extracts player/crosshair/information-state features, and produces explainable human-review risk reports.
acceptance_criteria: The generated project follows a docs-first layout with architecture, source authorization, data contracts, detection rationale, calibration limits, model card, and test plan before src implementation.

A built-in platform researcher discovers and refreshes official platform documentation, records cited capability profiles with freshness and authorization requirements, and produces reviewable adapter proposals for unknown platforms.

Platform acquisition uses explicit adapters for local files, authorized HTTPS downloads, Steam match-history sharing codes, and FACEIT-authorized demo links without hidden scraping or embedded credentials.

The parser normalizes real demoparser2 output and deterministic fixture input into one tick/event schema covering view angles, player positions, teams, shots, visibility or information state, deaths, and rounds.

Detection combines crosshair angular dynamics, target alignment, reaction timing, tracking, target switching, pre-aim/prefire, visibility, occlusion uncertainty, and information-relation signals into explainable evidence rather than a definitive cheating accusation.
A CLI runs download/import, parse, analyze, and JSON/HTML report workflows; synthetic legitimate and suspicious trajectories exercise the complete offline pipeline.
Generated tests, runtime evidence, quality report, and packaging checks pass through the existing Provider and post-build route.

product_backlog.title: Let the generated CS demo project create its own test video
product_backlog.outcome: The generated project can create an honest, reproducible synthetic evidence visualization video or render one from an authorized parsed input without pretending it is gameplay footage.
acceptance_criteria: A make-test-video CLI command produces WebM or MP4 from an internally generated synthetic scenario without requiring a demo download.
The renderer visualizes player positions, subject aim direction, target relationships, visibility or information state, shots, and timeline progression.
Every frame and sidecar manifest identify the output as synthetic evidence visualization rather than real gameplay or proof of cheating.
Authorized JSON or demoparser2-normalized inputs can be rendered through the same typed model; external inputs require an authorization assertion.
The command detects FFmpeg, validates the encoded media with FFprobe, records hashes and dimensions, and fails honestly when media tooling is unavailable.
Automated tests and one real generated video pass before local_packager rebuilds the canonical project bundle.

product_backlog.title: Let the generated CS demo project discover and test suitable inputs
product_backlog.outcome: The generated project autonomously finds bounded authorized candidates, ranks their evidence fitness, retries after failures, runs the full analysis and video workflow, and reports any synthetic fallback honestly.
acceptance_criteria: An auto-test CLI command discovers bounded local JSON, DEM, and safe ZIP candidates without crawling arbitrary locations.
Candidates are ranked using parseability, tick coverage, players, view angles, shots, visibility, information state, rounds, and map metadata.
A failed candidate is recorded and the next ranked candidate is attempted automatically.
The selected authorized real input runs the existing eight-stage pipeline and the existing evidence-video renderer without adding a generation or delivery route.
When no authorized real input succeeds, an explicitly enabled deterministic synthetic fallback runs the same workflow and is reported as PASS_WITH_LIMITS rather than a real-demo success.
The autonomous report redacts secrets, distinguishes discovery, execution, and evidence truth, and automated plus real CLI tests pass before local_packager rebuilds the bundle.

product_backlog.title: Autonomously discover and verify a public real CS2 demo
product_backlog.outcome: The generated project can opt into network discovery, enumerate a reviewed public demo catalog, verify current object identity and license provenance, download and safely extract a genuine CS2 demo, then prove it by parsing real ticks and player states through the existing workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Network discovery is explicit, bounded, rate-limited, and restricted to reviewed public catalogs or official credentialed platform APIs; it does not bypass authentication or scrape arbitrary sites.
The public catalog adapter dynamically enumerates current CS2 demo candidates and records repository, license, commit or object hash, download size, and expected content hash before acquisition.
Downloaded archives are HTTPS-only, size-bounded, hash-verified, and safely extracted without path traversal or unbounded member expansion.
A downloaded input is classified as a real demo only after demoparser2 parses non-zero ticks and player states; a downloaded file alone cannot pass.
The real demo runs through the existing analysis and evidence-video interfaces, and failed candidates automatically fall through to the next discovered source.
Automated tests, one actual public real-demo download and parse, canonical evidence, and local_packager inspection pass with limitations recorded honestly.

product_backlog.title: Validate generated modules before integration and delivery
product_backlog.outcome: Every generated component receives an independent language-aware quality validation after assembly, cached components are revalidated before reuse, and invalid module interfaces cannot be promoted as a passing project.
acceptance_criteria: A separate component quality-validation receipt is produced after module assembly and before the component can feed downstream generation.
JavaScript and TypeScript local imports and re-exports record exact symbols and reject missing exports, missing local re-export bindings, missing modules, and unimported sibling helpers.
Python syntax and implemented import interfaces plus JSON syntax are rechecked at component scope without relying on provider self-claims.
Previously passing component checkpoints are revalidated against the current quality contract before reuse.
The fully merged project receives an assembly quality validation and generation cannot report a passing quality gate when it fails.
The known broken CS Demo frontend is rejected while a valid split-module frontend, existing provider contracts, and kernel route guards pass.

product_backlog.title: Add design discovery and aesthetic quality to generated projects
product_backlog.outcome: Visual projects search real design references, select a coherent visual direction, feed a bounded design contract through the librarian, and fail generation when the implemented interface lacks the required design system or usable visual states.
acceptance_criteria: The existing Provider route runs a separate design-research stage after product and technical research for projects with a visual surface.

Design research records multiple source-backed references, three distinct directions, one selected direction, design tokens, interaction principles, accessibility constraints, and anti-copying boundaries.
Only a bounded design context enters frontend, media, and docs leaves through the existing generation-context librarian.
Design research artifacts are written before Provider source generation, and the generated project must include design_research.md and design_system.md before assembly can pass.
Frontend and assembled-project validation reject missing tokens, responsive behavior, focus treatment, interaction feedback, design documentation, or source-to-design traceability.
Design support receipts cannot authorize canonical visual evidence or public delivery PASS, and the Codex conversation Provider/local_packager route remains unchanged.

product_backlog.title: Prove large VN generation with self-generated art and story tree
product_backlog.outcome: A full-scale Provider trial generates and verifies a runnable visual-novel studio that creates distinct backgrounds and character sprites, edits and persists a branching story tree, binds generated assets to story nodes, and reports model or credential limitations honestly.
acceptance_criteria: The test uses the existing reviewed Provider component route with design research, bounded librarian context, module validation, post-build finalization, and no alternate generator.
The generated project contains docs-first product, architecture, interaction, image-generation, story-schema, quality, and test documentation plus a modular src and tests layout.
Users can create, edit, connect, branch, delete, persist, reload, and preview story nodes through one typed story-tree model.

Background and character-sprite generation are separate executable workflows that create distinct decodable image artifacts from user prompts and expose honest local-model or hosted-provider configuration checks.
Generated assets can be selected by characters or scenes and attached to story nodes without duplicating the story model in frontend and backend modules.

Generated-project unit, contract, integration, runtime, browser, accessibility, media-decoding, and design-quality checks pass or produce an evidence-backed canonical blocker rather than a false success.

product_backlog.title: Make canonical project planning goal-driven
product_backlog.outcome: Requirement decision emits one canonical GoalSpec and dynamic project plan that production Provider leaves and the controlled Agent Tree consume without generic Knowledge Studio fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Pomodoro, CSV cleaning, and visual-novel editor goals produce distinct capabilities, user flows, entities, business workstreams, leaf scopes, outputs, and test intents.
Unknown but sufficiently explicit goals receive a goal-derived plan or an explicit NEEDS_REWORK result, never an unrelated Knowledge Studio plan.
Knowledge Studio capabilities appear only when the user goal explicitly requests that product domain.
The Codex conversation Provider path consumes the canonical GoalSpec and project plan through its existing component and leaf context without adding a generation route.
Existing test, runtime, visual, review, packaging, and delivery truth semantics remain unchanged.

product_backlog.title: Bind dynamic project plans to goal acceptance
product_backlog.outcome: The existing post-build route evaluates every canonical goal test intent against an exact executable test and real passing test execution before a candidate can become review-ready.
acceptance_criteria: Each GoalDrivenProjectPlan assigns a stable exact test symbol to every acceptance behavior without changing the canonical GoalSpec truth.
The existing Provider tests component receives and implements those exact goal-test symbols through its current manifest and leaf route.
Post-build goal acceptance independently verifies plan identity, substantive executable tests, and a real passing test result before candidate review readiness.
Missing, trivial, mismatched, or failed goal tests produce NEEDS_REWORK and cannot be hidden by UI, fixture, packaging, or planning support artifacts.
Goal acceptance remains a support receipt and cannot authorize canonical final verdict, packaging, delivery receipt, or public delivery PASS.

product_backlog.title: Bind goal acceptance to canonical final verdict
product_backlog.outcome: Canonical final verdict independently checks applicable goal acceptance as a veto-only support prerequisite while every existing formal gate remains necessary for PASS.
acceptance_criteria: A production run with a frozen GoalDrivenProjectPlan requires a readable, self-consistent PASS CGKNGoalAcceptance receipt before Canonical Final Verdict can PASS.
Canonical Final Verdict independently rereads the goal specification, project plan, mapped candidate test sources, and receipt hashes instead of trusting the receipt status.
Missing, non-PASS, mismatched, or tampered applicable goal acceptance produces NEEDS_REWORK even when every formal gate reports PASS.
A passing goal-acceptance support receipt cannot replace any formal gate or promote a non-PASS formal-gate aggregate.
Legacy production runs without goal-plan artifacts preserve the existing final-verdict behavior, and Provider generation plus local_packager delivery routes remain unchanged.

product_backlog.title: Rebuild the CS2 demo anomaly lab with autonomous public-sample testing
product_backlog.outcome: A fresh generated project can discover reviewed public CS2 demo candidates online, verify and safely acquire one, parse real gameplay telemetry, and emit explainable player-level anomaly evidence for human review.
acceptance_criteria: The retired generated project, bundle, source cache, and runtime output are not reused; the replacement is created through the reviewed Provider generation route.

The project dynamically enumerates multiple candidates from a reviewed public HTTPS catalog and records public visibility, repository license, immutable commit, object identity, expected size, expected SHA-256, and every candidate attempt.

Acquisition is opt-in, bounded by requests, candidates, elapsed time, compressed and expanded bytes, and safe archive-member rules; authentication bypass, arbitrary-site crawling, traversal, symlinks, and unverified payloads are rejected.

A real input passes parser proof only when demoparser2 yields non-zero ticks and player states with positions and view angles; weapon_fire events are joined when present, and absent visibility or hearing telemetry remains unknown rather than inferred.

Analysis labels yaw and pitch deltas as a view-angle movement proxy rather than raw mouse input and reports player relationships, angular error, snap-before-shot, tracking, switching, and information-timing evidence only where source coverage supports each signal.

The CLI performs one real online discovery, download, extraction, parse, analysis, and JSON or HTML report run with synthetic fallback disabled, while unit and security tests prove candidate failover and acquisition boundaries.

Reports provide signal windows, coverage, confidence, provenance, limitations, and human-review guidance without automatic bans or definitive cheating accusations; unlabeled public demos cannot establish detection accuracy.
The generated project passes its tests and runtime checks, and only local_packager creates the canonical delivery bundle through the existing delivery route.

product_backlog.title: Verify and configure the hybrid local-model and API provider runtime
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN uses a verified API provider for formal generation and a measured Ollama configuration for bounded local support and registered fallback tasks without exposing credentials or adding a provider route.
acceptance_criteria: The installed Ollama service and selected code model complete strict-JSON small, medium, and component-manifest-scale requests through local_model_router with measured elapsed time.
The supplied API credential passes the existing provider smoke route with TLS verification and the configured formal-generation model, and a non-trivial structured request confirms usable quota.
Credentials are stored only in the supported current-user environment configuration, never in repository files, generated artifacts, logs, or commits.
Hybrid-safe routing keeps the reviewed API/provider route as formal generation owner while local support and registered fallback tasks use measured model, context, output, and timeout limits.
Provider, local-model routing, kernel, and credential-redaction tests pass after configuration, with any restart requirement documented.

product_backlog.title: Resume formal CS2 real-project verification and canonical delivery
product_backlog.outcome: The preserved CS2 generation run resumes through the reviewed API Provider route into an isolated formal candidate, then proves generated tests, a fresh bounded public-demo run, and canonical local_packager delivery truth without overwriting prior evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The prior formal run resumes only when its frozen goal hashes match, reuses only validated same-run Provider checkpoints, and writes to an isolated formal project directory without changing the already verified repaired project.
API Provider generation, semantic review, post-build finalization, and goal-acceptance evidence complete through the existing reviewed route with no alternate generator or fabricated identity.

The formal generated project passes its substantive pytest suite and one fresh opt-in online run discovers, verifies, downloads, safely extracts, parses, and reports on a genuine public CS2 demo with synthetic fallback disabled.

Runtime evidence preserves source commit, object hash and size, parser row/tick/player counts, event coverage, unknown information-state handling, view-angle proxy wording, human-review status, and NOT_EVALUATED detection accuracy.
Only local_packager may emit the final bundle and delivery_manifest; unmet identity, test, runtime, review, or delivery gates remain explicit non-PASS evidence.

product_backlog.title: Add a bounded Codex capability supervisor above librarian context
product_backlog.outcome: Codex can receive a compact librarian-curated escalation packet, diagnose capability gaps with tools, and return validated guidance to CGKN without becoming a second generator, formal evidence authority, or delivery exit.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic support contract bounds and hashes the goal, capability gap, librarian context, failure evidence, permitted outputs, and request budget before Codex sees them.

A Codex supervisor response can contain concise provider guidance, repair targets, acceptance checks, context requests, and tool-evidence requests, but cannot claim formal PASS, authorize delivery, package a project, or create source files in a sealed Provider candidate.

The existing agent_session and whiteboard remain the shared handoff surfaces, and the retained support pipeline can place the supervisor between context support and build work without changing Codex conversation default generation.
The project-local Codex skill is validated and one offline replay of the failed CLI generation produces a useful bounded response with zero external API calls.
Kernel, pipeline-manifest, schema, skill, and management regressions pass; local_packager remains the only delivery exit.

product_backlog.title: Evaluate the Codex capability brief on one concrete offline project
product_backlog.outcome: A bounded offline FocusForge experiment measures whether the supervisor brief produces a smaller, executable, goal-faithful project before any user-authorized Provider A/B run.
acceptance_criteria: The experiment is isolated from the Codex conversation default generation route and is explicitly labelled as an offline mock-Provider candidate with zero external API calls.
All nine requested FocusForge commands resolve to concrete callable handlers over a WorkItem, JSONRepository, and WorkspaceService domain contract.
The generated experiment stays within eight primary source files and five test files.
Generated tests and a real CLI smoke flow cover CRUD, filters and sorting, lifecycle transitions, summary, merge and replace import, export, corrupt storage, and duplicate IDs.
The result is compared with the preserved failed Provider baseline without claiming Provider token savings or formal delivery PASS.

product_backlog.title: Retire and rebuild the CS2 demo anomaly detector from a sealed project vision
product_backlog.outcome: The retired working source is replaced by a fresh reviewed-Provider project generated from durable defensive product vision, safety, truth, and acceptance contracts.
acceptance_criteria: The retired working project is converted into a durable product vision before its exact generated directory is removed, while historical artifacts and formal candidates remain preserved.
A fresh isolated output identity is generated only through the reviewed API Provider route with bounded Codex supervisor guidance and no retired-source reuse.
The fresh candidate passes compile and substantive security, parser, analysis, truth, report, and CLI tests.
A cached genuine authorized CS2 Demo completes parse-to-report without synthetic fallback and preserves NOT_EVALUATED accuracy, no automatic ban, and required human review.
Only local_packager may create a final bundle after canonical gates pass; Provider or runtime blockers remain explicit non-PASS evidence.

product_backlog.title: Feed a validated Codex capability brief into reviewed Provider generation
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN can generate a child project with bounded external Agent guidance while Provider ownership, formal evidence, packaging, and delivery authorities remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The formal CLI accepts only a hash-valid ready CGKNCodexCapabilityBrief with advisory-only authority.
Only a bounded projection reaches the existing Provider planning and component contexts, and the brief hash binds checkpoint reuse.
Tampered authority, changed resume identity, and oversized projections fail before Provider candidate generation.
A small child project is attempted through the reviewed Provider route and its generated tests plus CLI behavior are evaluated without manual source edits.
The change preserves Provider output validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, and delivery_manifest.json.

product_backlog.title: Package Agent-assisted CGKN for reuse across arbitrary projects
product_backlog.outcome: A user can install one companion CLI, initialize it in any local project, obtain a bounded Agent brief, and invoke the existing reviewed Provider generation route without copying secrets or creating another generation path.
acceptance_criteria: The companion is an independently installable Python package with a cgkn-agent command that works from an arbitrary project directory.
Project initialization writes only portable support configuration and a secret-ignored artifact directory under .cgkn.
Codex automation is explicit, ephemeral, read-only, schema-constrained, and fails visibly when the executable or authentication is unavailable.
Manual Agent drafts and Codex drafts pass through the same deterministic supervisor response and brief validation.
Project generation invokes only scripts/run_local_pipeline.py with a validated --codex-capability-brief and never stores API keys.
Package, unit, contract, Windows-path, and dry-run tests pass, with local Codex executable limitations reported honestly.

product_backlog.title: Connect Agent-assisted CGKN directly to Codex as a personal skill
product_backlog.outcome: Codex can discover and run the reviewed CGKN workflow from any local project without launching a nested Codex process.
acceptance_criteria: A validated use-cgkn skill is retained in the CGKN repository and discoverable from the user's global Codex skill location.
The skill initializes and prepares a target project through cgkn-agent, lets the active Codex task author only a bounded advisory draft, and seals it with the deterministic supervisor.
The skill does not launch nested codex exec, persist credentials, author a sealed Provider candidate, or add a generation or delivery path.
Explicit $use-cgkn invocation and implicit CGKN-specific routing are documented in UI metadata and tested in an isolated project.
Provider generation remains an explicitly requested follow-on through scripts/run_local_pipeline.py and real tests remain required before success is reported.

product_backlog.title: Expose CGKN as a personal Codex plugin with controlled MCP tools
product_backlog.outcome: Codex can call typed cgkn tools from any project through an installed personal plugin, while the existing Provider, evidence, packaging, and delivery authorities remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A valid cgkn personal plugin manifest and marketplace entry expose a local MCP server plus bounded companion instructions.

The MCP server provides typed project initialization, context preparation, brief sealing, generation planning/execution, test execution, and status inspection tools with explicit read/write annotations.
No MCP tool accepts an API key, invokes nested Codex, writes Agent-authored Provider candidate source, calls a packager directly, or adds a generation or delivery route.
Generation execution requires a hash-valid ready capability brief and explicit confirmation, then delegates only to scripts/run_local_pipeline.py.
Protocol-level MCP initialization, tool listing, positive tool calls, negative boundary cases, plugin validation, and applicable CGKN regressions pass.
After MCP pickup is verified in a fresh Codex task, the standalone global use-cgkn skill is retired or reduced to the plugin-bundled guidance.

product_backlog.title: Organize repository navigation, runtime-output boundaries, and local hygiene
product_backlog.outcome: Contributors can distinguish formal source, support evidence, examples, generated runtime output, and legacy material from one current guide while local caches no longer obscure the working tree.
acceptance_criteria: A current repository guide defines the purpose and retention rule for every top-level area without moving contract-bound evidence.
README navigation reflects plugins, tools, project management, formal evidence, runtime outputs, and legacy boundaries.
The small-scale plugin smoke run is retained under artifacts rather than presented as a reviewed example project.
Only verified untracked and reproducible cache or temporary directories are removed; tracked evidence and unrelated working changes are preserved.
A deterministic read-only hygiene check detects prohibited root caches, live CGKN support state under examples, and missing runtime ignore boundaries.
Management validation and applicable repository-hygiene tests pass.

product_backlog.title: Create an ACFV-reference-scale ORBIT-360 generated-project benchmark
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN has a runnable, documented test project that materializes and verifies 360 dependency-aware work units, supports resume and affected-closure repair, and remains clearly separate from formal delivery evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The project includes a Chinese project vision and a copy-paste usage guide that explain how it differs from and matches the ACFV reference scale.
The default plan contains exactly 360 deterministic work units arranged in dependency layers of width 35.
A real CLI run materializes all unit files, validates their hashes and dependencies, executes all units, and writes an inspectable run report.
Resume skips verified completed units, while repair of one unit recalculates only its transitive downstream closure.
The benchmark accepts no arbitrary command or generated code execution and labels its reports as support evidence rather than formal delivery PASS.
Unit and end-to-end tests pass against a real 360-unit workspace within a bounded local runtime.

product_backlog.title: Recover Codex-assisted Provider generation from quota and local fallback blockers
product_backlog.outcome: The existing Codex-assisted reviewed Provider route fails quickly on exhausted credentials, gives local code-generation fallback a bounded owner-aware runtime, and rejects a generated plan that drops the sealed brief's executable project contract.
acceptance_criteria: A non-retryable Provider key-usage-limit response cannot consume the full plugin subprocess budget through repeated identical semantic attempts; the exact pending leaf checkpoint remains recoverable.

A recorded local fallback for component generation receives the configured bounded local-generation timeout instead of the shorter API request timeout, while API-owned calls retain their existing cap.

A valid sealed Codex brief is hash-bound to the generation plan and its concrete package, module, public-symbol, entrypoint, safety, and acceptance constraints are checked before Provider file generation.
The ProjectPulse failure fixture rejects the observed backend/Note plan drift before source generation and accepts a plan that preserves the brief's projectpulse/Task/JSONRepository contract.
No fix writes a sealed generated candidate, adds a generation path, changes the Codex conversation default route, packages output, or promotes support evidence to formal PASS.
Targeted timeout, Provider failure, capability-brief, goal-plan, plugin, kernel, and management regressions pass.

product_backlog.title: Route Provider component manifests by interface complexity
product_backlog.outcome: Canonical multi-file component manifests use an interface-capable Provider model even when incidental payload accounting is small or unavailable, so the manifest does not discard GoalPlan paths before leaf generation.
acceptance_criteria: Initial component-manifest generation selects the configured interface-capable large model independently of small-payload downgrade logic.
Ordinary small component-generation payload routing remains available outside the component-manifest contract.
A regression reproduces the YanTu failure shape where a canonical backend owns many GoalPlan paths and verifies the manifest call route.
Exact canonical GoalPlan path ownership outranks generic frontend/backend directory guesses even when a package hint is present.
A high-complexity canonical Python leaf with many public symbols expands into safe same-directory bounded submodules that inherit only the exact parent ownership and retain independent checkpoints.
Provider-mainline, routing, kernel, and management validation pass without adding a generation or delivery path.

product_backlog.title: Make MCP resume diagnosis internally consistent
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN failure diagnosis reports one coherent resume decision: a complete current identity-bound pending plan is safe despite unrelated historical component drift, while legacy drift remains unsafe and Provider account blockers still require resolution before resume.
acceptance_criteria: resume.safe, resume.reason, and recommended_next_action cannot contradict one another.
A complete current identity-bound pending plan remains resumable when historical drift belongs to another component.
A legacy pending plan with active identity drift remains unsafe and recommends a fresh reviewed run.
Provider authentication or account availability failures recommend resolving the Provider before resuming the matching safe checkpoint.
Plugin, kernel, and management validations pass without changing generation or delivery authority.

product_backlog.title: Qualify Alibaba Bailian Qwen3.8-Max as a CGKN Provider
product_backlog.outcome: CGKN can diagnose and exercise Qwen3.8-Max through the existing OpenAI-compatible Responses route with bounded probe cost, no credential disclosure, and real generated-project test evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The built-in Provider probe reaches qwen3.8-max through the existing Responses route with a provider-compatible output budget and a visible pong response.
The Qwen probe disables reasoning only for the bounded diagnostic request, consumes no more than 128 output Tokens, and does not expose or persist the API key in project artifacts or tool arguments.
Provider transport, plugin, kernel-contract, and management validations pass without adding a generation or delivery path.
A live cgkn_probe_provider call reports connected while retaining formal evidence status NOT_EVALUATED.
An isolated minimal project is attempted through the reviewed Provider route and its supported tests are executed; any Provider or generation limitation is reported without formal PASS promotion.

product_backlog.title: Adapt Alibaba Qwen3.8 reasoning for bounded Provider leaves
product_backlog.outcome: Short deterministic CGKN leaf requests avoid Qwen3.8's default xhigh reasoning latency while retaining the reviewed Provider validation, checkpoint, packaging, and delivery route.
acceptance_criteria: Alibaba Model Studio qwen3.8 Responses generation payloads explicitly use reasoning effort none, while other providers and models retain their existing payloads.

Qualified Qwen component-file calls receive a deterministic compact request containing the target, direct interfaces, applicable contracts, bounded invariants/context, newest repair delta, implementation budget, and exact response shape while broad project state remains local.

Representative simple, dependency-aware, and oversized leaf fixtures prove material prompt reduction, a hard effective-request character ceiling, dynamic output budgets, and secret-free request-profile telemetry.
Provider responses continue through the unchanged local output, interface, implementation-depth, checkpoint, post-build, packaging, and delivery validators.
The bounded diagnostic probe keeps its existing 128-Token and reasoning-none behavior without credential disclosure.
Provider transport and kernel-contract tests cover the scoped reasoning policy and the reviewed Provider route remains unchanged.
The preserved identity-bound Qwen acceptance checkpoint is resumed through cgkn_generate and any complete candidate is tested through cgkn_test_generated.

product_backlog.title: Plan short requests as minimal parallel feature units
product_backlog.outcome: A request with one explicit function or command is planned as one bounded feature with frozen typed input, output, error, dependency, side-effect, acceptance, and file-ownership interfaces; independent features can then be built concurrently without generic workflow, persistence, or complexity inflation.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit single-operation Python CLI goal produces one canonical feature contract with one public entrypoint, exact typed inputs and output, declared errors and side effects, acceptance behaviors, owned paths, and no invented business capabilities.

Explicit negative scope such as no persistence, networking, frameworks, or unrelated features prevents repository, service, database, generic workflow, orchestrator, and pipeline outputs from entering the canonical plan.
The canonical plan freezes shared interfaces before generation and groups dependency-ready feature leaves into parallel batches only when their owned paths do not conflict.

Each Provider source request contains only one feature leaf plus its frozen contract and direct dependency interfaces; a rejected leaf is repaired independently without regenerating accepted unrelated leaves.

Minimal feature projects retain only necessary packaging, source, focused tests, and requested documentation while using the unchanged Provider validation, post-build, local_packager, public-delivery, and delivery-manifest route.
Planning, provider, kernel, and end-to-end regression tests prove the former one-function goal no longer expands into generic repository/service workflows.

product_backlog.title: Validate parallel feature leaves with a real postgraduate-exam assistant
product_backlog.outcome: A real standard-library postgraduate-exam assistant is generated from multiple frozen typed feature contracts, builds independent leaves concurrently, integrates them through one thin CLI, and passes focused project tests without unrequested product architecture.
acceptance_criteria: The goal freezes at least three explicit business feature contracts with exact typed inputs, outputs, errors, side effects, dependencies, owned paths, and acceptance checks.
At least two independent feature leaves share no owned paths and are scheduled in the same dependency-ready parallel batch.
One thin JSON CLI adapter depends on the independent feature leaves without redefining their business logic.
The generated project contains only standard-library source, one JSON CLI adapter, focused pytest tests, packaging metadata, and requested documentation.
A fresh reviewed Qwen run records leaf batches, repair scope, semantic-review metrics, and zero undeclared architecture.
